subject: surgery
title: Abdominal Aortic Aneurysm, EVAR and Carotid Disease

steps.tx: Permanent dilatation of the abdominal aorta beyond three centimetres is an **abdominal aortic aneurysm**. Most lie below the kidney arteries, called infrarenal aneurysms. They enlarge silently and are often found on scans for other problems. Early recognition matters because timely treatment gives clearly better outcomes than waiting for complications to develop first.
steps.say: An abdominal aortic aneurysm dilates the aorta beyond three centimetres, usually below the renal arteries.

vis.alt: Abdominal aortic aneurysm anatomy and rupture.
vis.caption: Abdominal aortic aneurysm. [Credit: StewardMD]

steps.tx: An aneurysm confined below the renal arteries is an **infrarenal aneurysm**. This position allows both open grafting and stent grafting in most patients. Aneurysms extending above the renal arteries are far more complex to treat. Students should connect this fact with the presenting symptoms, since examination questions usually test that clinical link directly.
steps.say: Infrarenal aneurysms sit below the renal arteries and allow standard open or stent repair.

steps.tx: Tearing of the aneurysm with bleeding into the abdomen is a **ruptured AAA**. Sudden abdominal or back pain with collapse and a pulsatile mass is the classic picture. Immediate resuscitation and emergency repair offer the only chance of survival. Documenting this finding clearly in the notes guides the next clinician and supports safe, well planned further management.
steps.say: A ruptured aneurysm causes sudden pain, collapse and a pulsatile mass needing emergency repair.

vis.alt: Abdominal aortic aneurysm on CT imaging.
vis.caption: Aneurysm on CT imaging. [Credit: StewardMD]

steps.tx: Repair from inside the aorta with a fabric covered stent is **EVAR**. Endovascular aneurysm repair avoids a large abdominal incision and suits older, frailer patients. Lifelong imaging surveillance watches for leaks around the graft. When this picture is seen in practice, urgent senior review is wise whenever there is any doubt about severity.
steps.say: EVAR repairs aneurysms from inside with a stent graft and needs lifelong leak surveillance.

vis.alt: EVAR stent graft and carotid endarterectomy.
vis.caption: EVAR and carotid surgery. [Credit: StewardMD]

steps.tx: Replacing the aneurysm with a sewn in fabric tube through an abdominal incision is **open aneurysm repair**. It is durable and needs little surveillance afterwards. Younger fit patients often prefer its long term reliability. Understanding this mechanism explains the symptoms, the investigation findings and the logic behind each step of treatment given.
steps.say: Open aneurysm repair sews in a durable fabric tube and needs little surveillance afterwards.

steps.tx: Ultrasound checks offered to men in their mid sixties form **aneurysm screening**. Finding aneurysms early allows planned repair before rupture. Small aneurysms enter surveillance with scans at intervals based on size. This distinction changes management, so it should be settled early rather than after empirical treatment has already begun.
steps.say: Aneurysm screening finds silent aneurysms early so repair is planned before rupture.

steps.tx: The commonest peripheral aneurysm, behind the knee, is a **popliteal aneurysm**. It threatens the leg through clotting and embolisation rather than rupture. Finding one prompts a search for an aortic aneurysm, and vice versa. Careful history taking and examination help place this finding in the right clinical context before treatment is planned.
steps.say: Popliteal aneurysms threaten the leg by clotting and prompt a search for aortic aneurysm.

steps.tx: An infected aneurysm caused by bacteria seeding the arterial wall is a **mycotic aneurysm**. Despite the name, bacteria rather than fungi usually cause it. Treatment combines prolonged antibiotics with surgical removal of infected tissue. Correlating this finding with imaging and laboratory results prevents both delayed treatment and unnecessary intervention in most patients.
steps.say: Mycotic aneurysms are infected arterial swellings, usually bacterial, needing antibiotics and surgery.

steps.tx: A contained leak held only by surrounding tissue, not arterial wall, is a **pseudoaneurysm**. It follows arterial puncture or trauma and pulsates with a bruit. Ultrasound guided compression or injection often seals smaller ones. Early recognition matters because timely treatment gives clearly better outcomes than waiting for complications to develop first.
steps.say: A pseudoaneurysm is a contained leak without arterial wall, often after puncture, sealed by compression or injection.

steps.tx: Splitting of the aortic wall layers with blood tracking between them is **aortic dissection**. Surgery replaces the ascending aorta in the dangerous type. Neck artery narrowing, carotid stenosis, is treated by endarterectomy or stenting to prevent stroke, while subclavian steal reverses arm flow to supply the brain.
steps.say: Aortic dissection splits the wall and needs ascending replacement, while carotid narrowing is cleared to prevent stroke.
